## What is a loop?

::: {.incremental}
- A loop is a element of that repeats a portion of code a desired number of
times
- Often with an iteration of values or variables
- Let's look at a simple sequence `seq(1:10)`
:::

## Using the sequence in a loop

This `seq(1:10)` gives us a simple sequence from one to ten

If we want to print out the sequences with 5 added to each we can loop

```{r}
for (i in seq(1, 10)) {
  # traditionally variables in a loop start at i
  # (they just do!)
  # what will happen is R will run the loop and for the first iteration
  # i will be 1 and then 2 and then 3 and so on
  i_plus_five <- i + 5
  result <- paste0(i, ' plus 5 equals ', i_plus_five)
  print(result)
}

```

## A loop's scope

::: {.incremental}
- Again, like functions a for loop does have global "scope"
- If you look `i_plus_five` exists in the global environment (top right of RStudio)
- But only in it's last value as it was overwritten each time
:::

## Using a vector of data

The real magic starts when we feed in a vector of data

```{r}
vector <- c('Bob', 'Pete', 'Mary')

for (i in vector) {
  result <- paste0('Hello ', i)
  print(result)
}
```

## Our function in a loop

::: {.incremental}
- So now we can look at running our function but within a loop
- But we need to recall that a function can only return one result
- So we would really like to collate all of those results into one object
- And we can do this by utilising a list object
- A list object is a super special multi dimensional thing that can contain a mix of variables, dataframes, plot objects and any combination thereof!
:::

## Lists need to be outlined

::: {.incremental}
- We can not create a list from within our loop, 
- otherwise we would be creating it blank on each iteration
- so lets make a blank list outside of our loop
:::

## Setting up the parts

First create an empty list

```{r}
plot_list <- list()
```

Then the vector we will feed to our loop

```{r}
vector <- c('RQM', 'RJ1', 'RDD')
```

Then using the function built in the previous section:

```{r}
for (i in vector) {
  plot_list[[i]] <- plot_site(i)
}
```

## Looking at the list

Let's call some of our plots from the list

```{r}
plot_list['RQM']

plot_list['RJ1']

```

It is also possible to call the plot from its position in the list

```{r}
plot_list[1]
```
